attacks.claim: The staff pilot is reported as completed with 0 misdelivered texts and shipped copy fixes, but the rollout schedules the pilot for Nov 2-6 and today is 2026-10-26, so these results cannot exist yet.
attacks.evidence: 'Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped' vs '1. Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above).'

attacks.claim: The carrier-level opt-in, STOP and HELP results are marked Pass, but they ran against the production provider account in test mode, which does not show real carrier delivery.
attacks.evidence: 'against the production SMS provider account in test mode' alongside 'Opt-in, YES confirm, STOP, HELP, re-opt-in (EN + ES) on 4 carriers | Pass'

attacks.claim: Locker accessibility features (high-contrast mode, audio guidance, adjustable text, ADA reach) are claimed but have no QA row. The accessibility testing covers only the web opt-in form.
attacks.evidence: 'screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack, and adjustable text size' vs QA row 'Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS' (no locker accessibility row)

attacks.claim: The opt-in form sends a confirmation text to any entered number with no stated rate limit, CAPTCHA, or per-number or per-IP throttle. It can be used to harass third parties or drain the SMS budget, and the 3-per-day cap covers only hold texts.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: abuse controls on the opt-in form. Flow step 2: 'We send a confirmation text; texts start only after the patron replies YES.'

attacks.claim: Staging ran against the production SMS provider account, so non-production environments hold live provider access. The artifact does not say how that account is isolated or whether test mode blocks sends to real patron numbers.
attacks.evidence: 'All QA ran on staging ... against the production SMS provider account in test mode'

attacks.claim: The guardian link that routes a juvenile's hold texts and pickup codes to another phone is not described as created or verified. Anyone who can attach as guardian could receive those messages.
attacks.evidence: 'guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account' with ABSENT: guardian-link creation, verification and authorization rules

attacks.claim: It is unclear whether guardian opt-in is limited to juvenile cards. If teen (13+) hold counts, pickup codes and locations can reach a parent's phone, that is a disclosure the teen has not consented to.
attacks.evidence: 'The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only; juvenile cards do not show it, and guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account.'

attacks.claim: The consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) has no stated retention period and is kept indefinitely while the flag is off. Only the notification log has a 30-day purge.
attacks.evidence: 'Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record' and 'Opt-in records are kept so turning the flag back on needs no re-consent.'

attacks.claim: Locker card-scan, PIN-entry, cell-open and lockout events tied to patron identity are new collection with no inventoried retention, access, or purge rule. The only stated purge covers the notification log.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention, access or purge rule for locker card-scan, PIN, cell-open or lockout records. Only purge stated: 'is purged after 30 days.'

attacks.claim: The locker vendor receives card identifiers and pickup events, but the artifact states no DPA or data-processing terms for it, while it documents one for the SMS provider.
attacks.evidence: 'The SMS provider is covered by our existing DPA (signed 2025-03)' vs ABSENT: data-processing terms for locker vendor receiving card number and PIN entry

attacks.claim: The artifact does not state where the SMS provider or locker vendor stores patron phone numbers, message logs or card-scan data, nor whether carriers and 10DLC aggregators are bound. Patron data may leave the county's jurisdiction without documented approval.
attacks.evidence: 'it retains message logs 30 days and is barred from marketing use'; ABSENT: provider hosting region, sub-processor chain, locker vendor data location

attacks.claim: No load, soak or concurrency testing appears in the QA table, yet the flags go on for ~210k cardholders at once and the announcement drives same-morning traffic to the account page.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: load or concurrency test. Rollout: 'Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders; announcement goes out at 10:00'

attacks.claim: Quiet-hours texts are all released at 08:00 with no send-rate limit or smoothing, which could exceed provider or 10DLC throughput and cause throttling or delivery failures.
attacks.evidence: 'Texts are sent only 08:00-20:00 patron local time; anything later is queued to 08:00.'

attacks.claim: Each bank holds 48 cells with no overflow rule. If holds assigned to lockers exceed free cells, the artifact does not say whether they are reassigned, queued or moved to the desk.
attacks.evidence: '3 locker banks (48 cells each)'; no overflow or cell-exhaustion behaviour described

attacks.claim: Spend-cap activation is not monitored. When the cap is reached, texts stop and every patron silently falls back, and the only alert is a 70% warning to ops.
attacks.evidence: 'On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back' vs Alerts: 'delivery failures > 5% for 15 min, webhook signature failures > 0, any locker bank offline > 10 min'

attacks.claim: No retry, dead-letter or per-message fallback is defined for failed deliveries. A provider degradation would only trip the 5%-for-15-minute alert, and holds could go unnotified without anyone knowing.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retry policy, dead-letter handling, or per-message fallback trigger on delivery failure

attacks.claim: sms_holds rollback does not say how queued or batched 08:00 texts are cancelled after the flag is turned off. Patrons could get SMS after rollback or duplicate notices through both channels.
attacks.evidence: 'sms_holds off: no new texts; every opted-in patron gets hold notices by their previous method' with no mention of queued or batched messages

attacks.claim: The locker rollback runs a live SQL remap with no stated idempotency, transaction or verification step. It was tested only on 1,200 rows, the production count is not given, and the manual shelf moves have no completion check.
attacks.evidence: 'remapped to the branch desk by scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql (tested in staging on 1,200 rows), staff move items to the holds shelf'

attacks.claim: For opt-ins made 'instead of' email, the 'no alert is lost' fallback depends on an email or phone channel still being on file and valid. The artifact does not verify contact-data currency for those patrons.
attacks.evidence: 'in addition to (or instead of) the current email' vs 'every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method ... so no alert is lost.'

attacks.claim: When several holds are batched, the artifact does not say how the single code and pickup location are chosen. Holds at different lockers or deadlines could produce a message that cannot be acted on correctly.
attacks.evidence: 'extra holds are batched into one message' and template 'Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913' with 'Codes are single-use'

attacks.claim: The mandated announcement says 'for every cardholder', but juvenile cards never see the SMS option. The required public wording is inaccurate.
attacks.evidence: 'Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder.' vs 'juvenile cards do not show it'

attacks.claim: The artifact states a language rule only for SMS. It does not say what language the locker touchscreen and audio guidance use, so Spanish-preferring patrons may get an English-only pickup kiosk.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: locker screen or audio-guidance language. Only stated: 'English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference.'

attacks.claim: Code generation (CSPRNG, length, entropy) and whether lockout is tracked per hold or per cell are not stated, so guessing resistance is unverified. The card scan or card-plus-PIN requirement limits the impact.
attacks.evidence: 'Code 482913' and 'wrong code x5 lock the cell' with ABSENT: code generation method and lockout scope

attacks.claim: Lock-screen or shared-device previews can reveal library holds at a specific branch along with a pickup code. There is no minimal-disclosure template.
attacks.evidence: 'Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14.'

attacks.claim: Card number plus PIN is entered on a public, unattended touchscreen with no stated shoulder-surfing mitigation.
attacks.evidence: 'enters card number + PIN, existing ILS PIN lockout applies'

attacks.claim: Shared or reassigned phone numbers may receive hold details and pickup codes meant for another household member. The artifact does not address reassigned numbers after opt-in.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: handling of shared or reassigned numbers after opt-in

attacks.claim: Queue depth appears on the dashboard but has no alert threshold, so a backlog during a provider slowdown or the 08:00 flush could go unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: 'Dashboard: ... queue depth' while Alerts omit queue depth

attacks.claim: A multi-hour locker outage outside desk hours has no defined patron-side fallback. Holds can be collected at the desk only during opening hours.
attacks.evidence: 'any locker bank offline > 10 min (pages branch manager + vendor; vendor SLA 4 h on-site)' and 'Holds stay collectible at the service desk during opening hours'

attacks.claim: No reconciliation is defined for locker cells whose items were not collected or not returned to the holds shelf.
attacks.evidence: 'returned to the holds shelf by staff next morning' with no reconciliation step

attacks.claim: The 2x hard cap has no per-day ceiling, so a runaway send loop could consume much of the budget before the 70% alert and fallback engage.
attacks.evidence: 'Provider account hard spend cap $900/month, alert to ops at 70%.'

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast and the $0.012 unit price have no stated basis (opt-in rate, holds per patron, batching) and no rate reference.
attacks.evidence: 'Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month' with ABSENT basis

attacks.claim: Phone-call fallback costs and load are not included in the SMS forecast, so spend at cap is unquantified.
attacks.evidence: 'every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call ...)'

attacks.claim: The spend-cap test used a $5 cap on the test-mode account, so the production $900 cap, the 70% alert delivery and billing halt are not verified.
attacks.evidence: 'Spend cap reached (test cap $5) → fallback to email / phone call | Pass'

attacks.claim: Spanish message and disclosure text are not shown in the artifact, so their wording and STOP/HELP accuracy cannot be reviewed.
attacks.evidence: 'English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference.' with ABSENT Spanish template text

attacks.claim: The example message says 'Oak St' while other text uses 'Oak Street', so branch naming may be inconsistent across channels.
attacks.evidence: '2 holds ready at Oak St locker' vs '24/7 pickup lockers at Oak Street'

attacks.claim: Reach requirements give only an upper bound. Lower bound and operability (one-hand use, fine motor demand) are not stated for the reader, touchscreen and cell doors.
attacks.evidence: 'Touchscreen and card reader mounted within ADA reach range (max 48 in)'

attacks.claim: Contrast is documented only for the locker screen. Contrast for the opt-in form, notification page and announcements is absent.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: contrast ratios for My Account > Notifications or announcement assets

attacks.claim: Assistive technology coverage is narrow (NVDA with Firefox and VoiceOver on iOS only). No TalkBack, JAWS or Safari desktop, and the pilot included no patrons with disabilities.
attacks.evidence: 'Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS'; 'Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds)'

attacks.claim: Patrons who opted into text because voice is inaccessible may fall back to an automated phone call, which they cannot use. The artifact does not address this.
attacks.evidence: 'email or automated phone call, which stays on file'

attacks.claim: The locker lockout after 5 wrong codes has no documented accessible recovery path beyond contacting staff, and no code-entry timeout or extension behaviour is stated.
attacks.evidence: '5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff'

attacks.claim: Accessibility of the branch posters and e-newsletter announcing the change is not addressed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility requirements for branch posters and e-newsletter

attacks.claim: Minor-consent and carrier 10DLC handling for teen (13+) cardholders is not addressed, and the artifact does not describe a reassigned-number check.
attacks.evidence: 'The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only'

attacks.claim: No ADA or Section 508 conformance report or WCAG level is cited for the public-facing locker and opt-in forms.
attacks.evidence: 'screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack' with no conformance reference

attacks.claim: Once the announcement is public at 10:00, a rollback at 09:00 or later would leave patrons told about a withdrawn feature.
attacks.evidence: 'Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders; announcement goes out at 10:00'

attacks.claim: Permanent SMS withdrawal deletes numbers and consent records within 30 days with no backup or hold, so reinstatement requires full re-consent.
attacks.evidence: 'If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days'

attacks.claim: Success is measured only by delivery, STOP rate, queue depth and locker status. No outcome metric such as pickup-within-deadline or missed-hold rate is defined.
attacks.evidence: 'Dashboard: texts sent, delivery rate, STOP rate, queue depth, locker cell status.'

attacks.claim: The usability evidence comes from 64 staff cards, which are unlikely to represent less digital cardholders.
attacks.evidence: 'Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds)'

attacks.claim: Lockers exist at three of 14 branches, yet the announcement goes to every cardholder. The artifact does not say how holds at non-locker branches are handled.
attacks.evidence: 'Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder. 24/7 pickup lockers at Oak Street, Millbrook and Harbor.'

attacks.claim: Every locker collection requires card scan or card-plus-PIN plus a code, with no shortcut for patrons who already hold the code.
attacks.evidence: 'The locker opens only after the patron scans their library card (or enters card number + PIN ...) AND enters the code.'

attacks.claim: Patrons who do not reply YES are silently dropped after 72 h and must restart the flow.
attacks.evidence: 'texts start only after the patron replies YES. Unconfirmed numbers are deleted after 72 h.'

attacks.claim: Quiet hours and batching can delay a hold-ready notice by hours, and no mitigation beyond the locker deadline is stated.
attacks.evidence: 'anything later is queued to 08:00. ... extra holds are batched into one message.'

attacks.claim: Codes expire at the pickup deadline, but the deadline is extended 3 days. The artifact does not say whether a new code is issued or what the extension notice contains.
attacks.evidence: 'Codes are single-use, expire at the pickup deadline' and 'the hold is extended 3 days'

attacks.claim: Quiet hours, daily cap, batching and language selection are specified for SMS only. The artifact does not say whether they reuse the existing hold-notification pipeline, which risks divergent code paths.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: whether SMS shares the existing hold-notification pipeline

attacks.claim: Column encryption, the 30-day purge job and the 4 h vendor SLA are stated as fact without cited test or contract evidence.
attacks.evidence: 'the phone column uses the same column encryption as the existing email field'; 'vendor SLA 4 h on-site'

attacks.claim: Flags go to all ~210k cardholders at 09:00 with no canary percentage and no stated rollback thresholds for the first hours.
attacks.evidence: 'Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders'

attacks.claim: SMS depends on one provider with no documented second provider or exit plan, and locker hardware and control software come from one vendor with no data export or replacement plan.
attacks.evidence: 'the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA'; 'installed and acceptance-tested by the vendor'

attacks.claim: The artifact does not say whether the provider receives a deletion instruction or confirmation on withdrawal, so removal of patron phone data from the vendor cannot be verified.
attacks.evidence: 'numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days' with ABSENT: vendor deletion confirmation
